name: Stratacite-VL
description: A functionally layered ceramic-composite armor system consisting of alternating hard-face boron carbide strike plates, energy-absorbing alumina-fiber interlayers, and compliant polymer backing bonded through nano-scale adhesion chemistry that prevents delamination under repeated impact. The architecture is tuned so that each layer performs a distinct function: the strike face shatters and erodes the projectile, the interlayers absorb and redistribute the shock wave, and the backing captures spall and prevents penetration of fragmentation. Tessera Materials produces Stratacite-VL in standardized modular panels that can be field-assembled into custom configurations.
applications: military and law enforcement body armor inserts
personnel protective equipment for high-risk extraction
story_hooks: A Tessera Materials quality control failure has produced a batch of Stratacite-VL where the interlayer adhesion chemistry was applied at the wrong temperature — the panels look and test identically but will delaminate catastrophically on the third impact.

A black-market fabricator has cracked the Stratacite-VL layering architecture and is producing near-equivalent panels at a third of the cost, undercutting Tessera's military contracts — both Tessera and the military want the operation found.

A journalist has obtained footage showing Stratacite-VL panels being sold directly to a sanctioned paramilitary organization through a shell distributor — following the supply chain leads somewhere deeply inconvenient.
